**Observations from the image:**

- **Plant part affected**: Leaf (broad, dark green leaf — likely tomato or a solanaceous plant)
- **Lesion characteristics**:
  - Multiple dark gray-to-black necrotic spots scattered across the leaf surface
  - Spots range from small to medium in size, with irregular to roughly circular outlines
  - Some lesions show faint concentric ring patterning (target-board appearance)
  - Darker margins with slightly lighter/grayish centers on several spots
  - Fine granular/sandy debris visible on leaf surface (could be pycnidia or environmental)
- **No obvious**: white fuzzy mycelium (Gray Mold/Sclerotinia), white powdery coating (Powdery Mildew), water-soaked margins (Late Blight), or mosaic/mottling (virus)

**Reasoning through top candidates:**

- **Early Blight** (*Alternaria solani*): Produces dark brown-to-black spots with concentric rings and sometimes yellow halos on tomato. The irregular-to-angular dark lesions with hints of concentric patterning fit well.
- **Septoria Leaf Blotch**: Typically very small, uniform circular spots with light tan centers, dark borders, and clearly visible pycnidia — the spots here appear larger and more irregular.
- **Anthracnose**: Dark sunken lesions, more commonly on fruit than leaves; possible but less typical.
- **Bacterial Speck**: Very small, pinpoint-to-small black spots usually with yellow halos — these spots appear larger.

The size, shape, dark coloration, irregular-to-circular outline, and faint concentric ring pattern on what appears to be a solanaceous leaf points most strongly to **Early Blight**.
